RED, AND THE REASON THIS NOTE CARRIED IS DEAD: NOTHING IS GRADED AS WIRED THAT IS NOT. ic's instrument fix (5bd42c95) replaced `unwired_families()` with `wiredness()`, which DRIVES every shipped entry for itself through `dispatch::shipped_entries` and keys the deferral on the ENTRY PATH rather than on the first path token. The old form probed only each family's bare parent, so `st bootstrap`'s three flags were graded wired because `st` is. Driven result, 6/6 green: DEFERRED 20, NOT PROBED 3, GATED 102 with the gate able to fire for 32, RATCHET 3. THE PREDICTION WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN AND ITS UNPREDICTED HALF IS THE PART THAT COUNTS. ic predicted the st bootstrap trio would move and predicted the MIRROR ERROR -- families whose ROOT is unwired but whose LEAVES are wired, deferred wholesale. It fired twice: `agents init --template` was named in advance; `llm usage_rules --symlink` was NOT, because ic did not know `llm`'s root refuses bare. Recorded as the unpredicted half rather than folded into the predicted one, which is what makes the prediction evidence at all -- a prediction that absorbs its misses measures nothing. Both verified genuinely unread against the source rather than the roster: `llm_usage_rules()` takes no ArgMatches (render.rs:6452), and `template` is spelled nowhere in the crate. WHY IT STAYS RED: the criterion's words are READ, OR WITHDRAWN, and three declared-and-unread flags on WIRED entries are neither. One is ratified (`ingest --from-md`); two are open scope decisions filed as 0180 (`agents init --template`, dc/ST0058) and 0181 (`llm usage_rules --symlink`, WP-09/ic). A RATCHET WITH OWNERS IS THE MECHANISM FOR REACHING THE CRITERION, NOT THE CRITERION SATISFIED -- greening on the ratchet's existence would certify the process instead of the property. 0180 is RULED WITHDRAWN (vc, 2026-08-31): nothing was ever built behind the flag, so withdrawing removes a FALSE CLAIM rather than a feature, and `AC-06.8`'s own remedy sanctions both directions. 0181 is NOT the same question and must not be swept in with it -- v2's `--symlink` linked `usage-rules.md` rather than copying it, so if the capability EXISTED and did not survive the port, retiring it quietly would record a loss as a tidy-up, and that is hv's call. MOVES WHEN 0181 is decided and both flags are read or withdrawn.

**GREEN 2026-09-09 (vc, on cc's build at `ff9192746`; driven independently before the row was moved, not taken off cc's report).** `cargo test -p intent-cli --test suite flag_reachability`: **6/6 arms, `0 flag(s) DECLARED and unread on a wired family`.** The ratchet is empty because the last member was RESOLVED, not exempted: `ingest --from-md` moved `keep` -> `retire`, and the hand-listed exception that had been holding the suite up came OUT with the flag rather than being emptied -- which is what stops this green needing a footnote.

**THE ROW'S OWN INSTRUMENT DECLARES A REACH LIMIT AND THE ROW NOW CARRIES IT, WHICH IS THE CONDITION THIS CLOSE WAS GRANTED ON.** cc raised it against their own delivery. Printed on every run: **113 flags examined across the wired families; the gate CAN fire for 32 and CANNOT for 81 whose id also appears elsewhere in the renderer.** A further 32 of the gated are held only by the coincidence that nothing else spells their id. **So `0 unread` is a true statement about what this check can see, and NOT the statement _every declared flag is read_.** The limit is printed rather than hidden, which is what makes it declarable instead of a hole.

**AND THE SHIELDED CLASS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL -- IT ATE ONE OF THIS ROW'S OWN FIVE NAMED INSTANCES.** `st new -s` sat in the shielded 81 because its long spelling is `start`, and that string is all over the renderer as a verb, so a grep found the spelling it asked for while the claim had another one. **The row's original census missed it for exactly that reason, and cc closed it by DRIVING A VARIATION rather than reading the green**: on a fresh scratch project at HEAD, one command apart, `st new "started thread" -s` lands `WIP` and `st new "plain thread"` lands `Triage`. The flag is wired; the row's text saying it lands at Triage with no effect is stale prose about a fixed defect.

**THE RULING THAT EMPTIED THE RATCHET IS RECORDED AT `AC-06.8`'s SUBJECT AND REVERSED ITS AUTHOR.** vc ruled `--from-md` `keep` on 2026-08-15 over ic's objection that it is a mode flag with one mode, on the ground that withdrawal would contradict ratified rows at `AC-10.2`/`AC-10.3`. **Driven 2026-09-09: those two rows contain ZERO occurrences of the flag, and the four artefacts ic cited then no longer cite it at all.** The premise had evaporated on both legs, so the ruling was overturned in ic's favour. `intrinsic` was explicitly refused as the disposition -- its ratified gloss is *ships, and clap supplies it*, which is false of a domain flag, and using it would have made the row green by describing the flag as something it is not.

**ONE RESIDUE DELIBERATELY NOT SWEPT INTO THIS CLOSE:** `docs/reference/commands.md` still advertises `--from-md`, because `gen_reference.sh` rewrites 17 files carrying ten days of other nodes' unregenerated landings, and committing that under this row would hide their changes inside it. Routed to vc as its own act.
